title: Do animals have a sixth sense?
summary: Josh and Chuck explore whether animals have a "sixth sense," starting with Oscar, a cat at the Steere House Nursing and Rehab Center in Rhode Island that reportedly sits with patients shortly before they die (a 2007 New England Journal of Medicine account; the hosts checked by phone that Oscar is alive). They discuss smell as a likely explanation, then dogs detecting cancer (a 2006 study with lung and breast cancer patients and breath samples, plus bladder cancer in urine), animal hearing range, animals reacting before the 2004 tsunami, and seizure alert dogs, including Canine Assistance in Alpharetta, Georgia, and a neurologist's view that dogs respond to early seizure signs rather than predicting them. The episode closes with listener mail correcting the high fructose corn syrup discussion: US sugar import quotas kept sugar prices high, which pushed soft drink makers toward HFCS.

segments.title: Opening banter and sponsor tag
segments.summary: Josh and Chuck open with casual banter about cats and a sponsor-style intro before turning to the topic of cats that predict death.

segments.title: Oscar the cat predicts death
segments.summary: The hosts describe Oscar, a cat at a Rhode Island nursing home who reportedly sits with patients shortly before they die, based on a 2007 New England Journal of Medicine account. They debunk an internet rumor that Oscar was killed, saying a phone call confirmed he is alive.
topics: Steere House Nursing and Rehab Center

segments.title: Smell as explanation for predicting death
segments.summary: The hosts discuss smell as the likeliest explanation for Oscar's behavior, suggesting chemicals released as body cells break down could attract the cat.

segments.title: Dogs detecting cancer
segments.summary: The hosts cite a 2006 study in which dogs sniffed breath samples from lung and breast cancer patients and healthy controls with high accuracy, plus another study on dogs detecting bladder cancer in urine. Anecdotes of dogs detecting breast cancer and a freckle that turned out to be skin cancer are also mentioned.

segments.title: Animal hearing and the sixth sense explanation
segments.summary: The hosts explain that animals often have heightened senses, such as hearing ranges above human limits, which may explain reported weather and earthquake predictions. They also mention animals acting strangely before the 2004 tsunami.

segments.title: Seizure alert dogs
segments.summary: The hosts discuss dogs that alert to epileptic seizures, including a CNN-reported woman who has a seizure alert dog. A neurologist, Gregory Berkley, argues dogs respond to early signs before the patient is aware, rather than predicting seizures. Canine Assistance in Alpharetta, Georgia trains these dogs, and the hosts note a dog's seizure history and that the training is costly.

segments.title: Closing thoughts on animal senses
segments.summary: The hosts note that dog seizure alerts are unproven and not a fail-safe, and that people should be cautious about paying large sums to breeders or trainers.

segments.title: Listener mail: high fructose corn syrup and sugar quotas
segments.summary: A listener from Los Angeles explains that US sugar import quotas and tariffs keep domestic sugar prices high, which led soft drink makers to switch to high fructose corn syrup after President Reagan lowered the sugar quota in the 1980s.
